newsitem.title: USA: Security threat at U.S. Jewish headquarters.
newsitem.headline: Security threat at U.S. Jewish headquarters.

text.p: A mailed package containing suspicious "biological material" sparked a major security alert at the headquarters of the Jewish organisation B'nai B'rith on Thursday, bringing police, firemen, the FBI and military disposal squads to the scene.

No serious injuries were initially reported but at least two B'nai B'rith employees were reported to have suffered respiratory problems. One person was seen being sprayed with a decontaminant by a white-clad rescue team.

The building in bustling downtown Washington D.C. about six blocks from the White House was evacuated and streets blocked, sowing chaos in the capital. U.S. military disposal experts gingerly removed the suspicious package in a cannister for examination at a nearby naval medical laboratory.
"We found some biological material and a note that was left with the package," District of Columbia Police Chief Larry Soulsby said in a televised interview.
"An 8X10 envelope was found in our mailroom with red liquid coming out of it" late Thursday morning, B'nai B'rith spokeswoman Robin Schwartz-Kreger told Reuters by telephone.
She said it was accompanied by a "threatening" letter but she did not know the nature of the threats.

Deputy Fire Chief Donald Edwards said in an interview with the local NBC News affiliate that the package sent to the B'nai B'rith mailroom contained a gelatin-like substance with a reportedly pungent aroma.

"We don't know what it is, and to find out what it is, so that we can mitigate the incident properly, we contacted several people, to include CDC (the federal Centres for Disease Control in Atlanta) as well as ... a national chemical organisation that tracks the movement of chemicals throughout the nation and the world," Edwards said.

FBI spokeswoman Susan Lloyd told Reuters the agency was analysing the letter that came with the package, which consisted "of a yellow mailing envelope and a container that looks like a petri dish with cellophane around it."
